```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(patchwork)
library(htmltools)
source(here("R", "functions.R"))

render_details_cell <- function(text, label = "Read abstract") {
    vapply(
        text,
        function(x) {
            if (is.null(x) || is.na(x) || !nzchar(trimws(x))) {
                return("Unavailable")
            }

            cleaned <- trimws(x)
            cleaned <- gsub("\\s+", " ", cleaned)
            cleaned <- htmlEscape(cleaned)

            paste0(
                '<details class="project-details"><summary>',
                label,
                '</summary><div class="project-detail-body">',
                cleaned,
                '</div></details>'
            )
        },
        character(1)
    )
}

add_miga_ellipsis <- function(text) {
    vapply(
        text,
        function(x) {
            if (is.null(x) || is.na(x) || !nzchar(trimws(x))) {
                return(NA_character_)
            }

            cleaned <- trimws(x)
            if (grepl("[.!?…]$", cleaned)) {
                return(cleaned)
            }

            paste0(cleaned, "…")
        },
        character(1)
    )
}

ibrd_annual <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "ibrd_annual.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
ibrd_period <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "ibrd_by_period.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
ibrd_proj <- read_csv(
    here("data", "processed", "ibrd_projects.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
instr_period <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "instrument_by_period.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
sec_period <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "sector_by_period.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
sec_totals <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "sector_totals.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
top10 <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "ibrd_top10.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
theme_pres <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "abstract_themes.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
word_counts <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "word_counts.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
ifc_proj <- read_csv(
    here("data", "processed", "ifc_projects.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
ifc_sector <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "ifc_by_sector.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
miga <- read_csv(
    here("data", "processed", "miga_projects.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
wdi <- read_csv(
    here("data", "derived", "wdi_scope.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
deflator <- read_csv(
    here("data", "processed", "us_gdp_deflator.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)

period_levels <- c(
    "1980–1989",
    "1990–1999",
    "2000–2009",
    "2010–2019",
    "2020–2025"
)

ibrd_scope <- ibrd_proj |>
    filter(
        !is.na(approval_year),
        approval_year >= 1980,
        approval_year <= 2025
    ) |>
    mutate(period = factor(period, levels = period_levels))

api_raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
    here("data", "raw", "world_bank_costa_rica_filtered.json"),
    simplifyDataFrame = FALSE
)
api_abstracts <- tibble::tibble(
    project_id = vapply(
        api_raw[["projects"]],
        function(p) as.character(p[["id"]]),
        character(1)
    ),
    project_abstract = vapply(
        api_raw[["projects"]],
        function(p) {
            entry <- p[["project_abstract"]]
            if (is.null(entry) || length(entry) == 0) {
                return(NA_character_)
            }
            if (!is.null(entry[["cdata!"]])) {
                return(as.character(entry[["cdata!"]]))
            }
            if (!is.null(entry[["cdata"]])) {
                return(as.character(entry[["cdata"]]))
            }
            NA_character_
        },
        character(1)
    )
)

instr_period <- instr_period |>
    filter(period %in% period_levels) |>
    mutate(period = factor(period, levels = period_levels))
```

## B. Nominal versus real: the inflation story

```{r fig8}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "fig8_nominal_vs_real.png"))
```

In real 2025 dollars, the eight 1980s operations (~$294M nominal total) represented approximately **`r scales::dollar(ibrd_period$real_principal[ibrd_period$period=="1980–1989"], scale=1e-6, suffix="M", accuracy=1)`** — substantially larger than the nominal figure suggests. Of that total, three policy-based adjustment operations (SAL I, SAL II, and the Export Development loan) accounted for roughly $205M nominal, or about 70% of the decade's lending. The 2009 $500M DPL was approximately $728M in 2025 dollars. The recent 2020–2025 operations lose some of their comparative magnitude once inflation-adjusted.

*Real amounts use the US GDP deflator (NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS, base 2020=100). The 2025 deflator value is preliminary.*

## C. Instrument mix

```{r fig2}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "fig2_instrument_mix.png"))
```

```{r instr-table}
#| echo: false
instr_period |>
    group_by(period) |>
    mutate(pct = round(100 * total_principal / sum(total_principal), 0)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(
        total_principal = fmt_millions(total_principal),
        real_principal = fmt_millions(real_principal)
    ) |>
    select(
        Period = period,
        Instrument = instrument_group,
        N = n,
        `Nominal (US$M)` = total_principal,
        `Real 2025 (US$M)` = real_principal,
        `% of period` = pct
    ) |>
    kable(
        caption = "Instrument mix by period — DPL vs Investment Project Financing"
    ) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
```

**Instrument classification note:** Structural Adjustment Loans (SAL I, SAL II, SAL III) are classified as Development Policy Lending. The Export Development loan (1983, P006922) is classified as adjustment-era policy lending via a manual override in `data/manual/instrument_overrides.csv`. The 1980 Highway Project (P006919) carries an NPL loan-type code but is classified as Investment Project Financing — its abstract confirms it financed road rehabilitation and equipment, not policy conditions (also a manual override). The Catastrophe DDO (2008), Public Finance and Competitiveness DPL-DDO (2009), and all Fiscal and Decarbonization DPLs (2020–2025) are Development Policy Loans. All others are Investment Project Financing or equivalent.

## D. Sectoral composition

```{r fig3}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "fig3_sector_composition.png"))
```

```{r sector-table}
#| echo: false
sec_totals |>
    mutate(
        alloc_principal = fmt_millions(alloc_principal),
        alloc_real = fmt_millions(alloc_real)
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", alloc_principal)))) |>
    select(
        `Sector group` = sector_group,
        Allocations = n_allocations,
        Projects = n_projects,
        `Allocated (nominal)` = alloc_principal,
        `Allocated (real 2025)` = alloc_real,
    ) |>
    kable(
        caption = "Sector group totals (allocated where sector percentages available)"
    ) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
```

> **Two distinct coverage figures:** Sector *metadata* is available for **22 of 35** in-scope projects, whose combined original principal is approximately **$2.7 billion** (~59% of the $4.6B total). However, not all of those projects have complete sector *percentages* — only projects with reliable allocation percentages contribute to the dollar totals shown here. The actual amounts allocated across the sector categories sum to roughly **$2.2 billion**, the difference being projects with sector names but missing or zero percentages. The 2020–2025 DPL series largely lacks sector percentages in the API; it is excluded from allocation calculations. P178320 (COVID-19 Vaccines, Terminated, $0 original principal) is excluded from dollar totals. Sector allocations are a partial, non-representative view of the portfolio — treat with appropriate caution.

## E. Development priorities in project language

```{r fig5}
#| fig-cap: "Theme keyword presence by period. Only periods with available abstracts are shown. The 1990–1999 period has zero project abstracts in the API and is excluded. Percentages are shares of projects WITH available abstracts that mention the theme."
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "fig5_abstract_themes.png"))
```

For additional detail, see the [top 30 words](#top-30-words) identified in the project abstracts.

```{r theme-table}
#| echo: false
theme_labels <- c(
    "Infrastructure" = "Infrastructure",
    "Environment_Climate" = "Environment & Climate",
    "Social_Development" = "Social Development",
    "Governance_Fiscal" = "Governance & Fiscal",
    "Competitiveness_Trade" = "Competitiveness",
    "Disaster_Risk" = "Disaster Risk"
)
theme_pres |>
    filter(!is.na(period)) |>
    mutate(theme_label = theme_labels[theme]) |>
    select(
        Period = period,
        Theme = theme_label,
        `Abstracts available` = n_with_abstract,
        `Total IBRD projects` = n_total_ibrd,
        `With theme` = n_with_theme,
        `% of abstracts` = pct
    ) |>
    kable(
        caption = "Thematic keyword presence in project abstracts by period. '% of abstracts' is the share of projects with available abstracts that mention the theme — NOT the share of all in-scope projects. The 1990–1999 period has no abstracts in the API extract."
    ) |>
    kable_styling(
        bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"),
        font_size = 11
    ) |>
    collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
```

> **Abstract coverage and interpretation:** The 1990–1999 period has **zero** project abstracts available in the WB Projects API extract. Other periods: 1980–1989: **2 abstracts of 8 projects**; 2000–2009: **7 of 7**; 2010–2019: **1 of 2**; 2020–2025: **9 of 12**. The 1980s and 2010s figures are extremely sparse — drawing conclusions from 2 or 1 abstract respectively is inadvisable. Percentages are shares of projects *with available abstracts*, not all in-scope IBRD projects.
>
> **What the table does and does not tell us:** Infrastructure language appears at 100% in every period with available abstracts — but this reflects keyword matching (the words "road", "transport", "energy" appear widely), not that every project was an infrastructure investment. Environment/Climate keywords appear in the 2000s (57%) and 2020s (89%) but are absent in the 1980s (0%) and 2010s (0% from a single abstract). Governance/Fiscal language is absent in the 1980s, then consistently present from the 2000s onward. These patterns reflect stated language in project abstracts — not project expenditure, project effects, or Bank institutional priorities more broadly.

## F. Economic and development context

```{r fig6}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "fig6_development_trajectory.png"))
```

```{r wdi-table}
#| echo: false
wdi |>
    filter(
        year %in%
            c(1980, 1985, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2023, 2024)
    ) |>
    mutate(
        gdp_per_capita_usd = scales::dollar(gdp_per_capita_usd, accuracy = 100),
        gdp_growth_pct = ifelse(
            is.na(gdp_growth_pct),
            "—",
            paste0(round(gdp_growth_pct, 1), "%")
        ),
        gini = ifelse(is.na(gini), "—", round(gini, 1)),
        life_expectancy_years = ifelse(
            is.na(life_expectancy_years),
            "—",
            round(life_expectancy_years, 1)
        )
    ) |>
    select(
        Year = year,
        `GDP per capita` = gdp_per_capita_usd,
        `GDP growth` = gdp_growth_pct,
        Gini = gini,
        `Life expectancy` = life_expectancy_years
    ) |>
    kable(
        caption = "Costa Rica selected WDI indicators (contextual only). GDP per capita is current US dollars — not inflation-adjusted. Life expectancy is available through 2024; 2025 is not yet published. Gini: 2024 value is 45.8; a preliminary 2025 estimate (45.5) is available from the WB API but may be revised."
    ) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
```

## Appendix

### All in-scope IBRD projects {#ibrd-projects}

```{r all-projects-table}
#| echo: false
ibrd_html <- ibrd_scope |>
    arrange(approval_year) |>
    left_join(api_abstracts, by = "project_id") |>
    mutate(
        total_principal = fmt_millions(total_principal),
        real_principal_2025 = fmt_millions(real_principal_2025),
        net_principal = fmt_millions(net_principal),
        Abstract = render_details_cell(project_abstract, "Read abstract")
    ) |>
    select(
        `Project ID` = project_id,
        `Project name` = project_name,
        Year = approval_year,
        `Nominal` = total_principal,
        `Real 2025` = real_principal_2025,
        `Net` = net_principal,
        `Instrument` = instrument_group,
        Abstract,
        `Status` = loan_status_summary
    )

withTags({
  table(
    class = "table table-striped table-condensed",
    caption = "All IBRD in-scope projects, 1980–2025 (nominal and real 2025 USD)",
    thead(
      tr(
        th("Project ID"),
        th("Project name"),
        th("Year"),
        th("Nominal"),
        th("Real 2025"),
        th("Net"),
        th("Instrument"),
        th("Abstract"),
        th("Status")
      )
    ),
    tbody(
      lapply(seq_len(nrow(ibrd_html)), function(i) {
        row <- ibrd_html[i, ]
        tr(
          td(row[["Project ID"]]),
          td(row[["Project name"]]),
          td(as.character(row[["Year"]])),
          td(row[["Nominal"]]),
          td(row[["Real 2025"]]),
          td(row[["Net"]]),
          td(row[["Instrument"]]),
          td(HTML(as.character(row[["Abstract"]]))),
          td(row[["Status"]])
        )
      })
    )
  )
})
```

### All in-scope IFC investment projects {#ifc-projects}

```{r ifc-table}
#| echo: false
ifc_html <- ifc_proj |>
    filter(is_investment, in_scope, !is_pipeline) |>
    arrange(best_year) |>
    mutate(
        amt_m = ifelse(
            is.na(ifc_invest_usd_m),
            "—",
            paste0("$", ifc_invest_usd_m, "M")
        ),
        Description = render_details_cell(description, "Read description")
    ) |>
    select(
        `Project #` = project_number,
        `Project name` = project_name,
        `Ind. year` = best_year,
        `Date type` = date_type,
        `IFC own-acct` = amt_m,
        Sector = sector_group,
        Description,
        Status = status
    )

withTags({
  table(
    class = "table table-striped table-condensed",
    caption = "IFC investments in Costa Rica (indicative dates; amounts in nominal USD)",
    thead(
      tr(
        th("Project #"),
        th("Project name"),
        th("Ind. year"),
        th("Date type"),
        th("IFC own-acct"),
        th("Sector"),
        th("Description"),
        th("Status")
      )
    ),
    tbody(
      lapply(seq_len(nrow(ifc_html)), function(i) {
        row <- ifc_html[i, ]
        tr(
          td(row[["Project #"]]),
          td(row[["Project name"]]),
          td(as.character(row[["Ind. year"]])),
          td(row[["Date type"]]),
          td(row[["IFC own-acct"]]),
          td(row[["Sector"]]),
          td(HTML(as.character(row[["Description"]]))),
          td(row[["Status"]])
        )
      })
    )
  )
})
```

> **Date caveat:** Only 2 IFC projects (Advisory Services) have actual Approval Dates. All investment projects show Projected Board Dates — planned, not confirmed. Year assignments are approximate. Do not use for precise annual trend analysis.

### MIGA historical guarantees

```{r miga-table}
#| echo: false
names(miga) <- gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "_", tolower(names(miga)))
names(miga) <- gsub("_+", "_", names(miga))
names(miga) <- gsub("_$", "", names(miga))
miga_html <- miga |>
    arrange(fiscal_year) |>
    mutate(
        gross_exposure_up_to = paste0("$", gross_exposure_up_to, "M"),
        Description = render_details_cell(add_miga_ellipsis(description), "Read description")
    ) |>
    select(
        `Proj. ID` = project_id,
        Title = title,
        Sector = sector,
        `FY` = fiscal_year,
        `Peak exposure` = gross_exposure_up_to,
        Description,
        `Investor country` = investor_country
    )

withTags({
  table(
    class = "table table-striped table-condensed",
    caption = "MIGA historical guarantees in Costa Rica (deduplicated; project 3639 shown at FY2003 maximum). 'Peak exposure' = maximum MIGA liability under issued contracts, not a loan.",
    thead(
      tr(
        th("Proj. ID"),
        th("Title"),
        th("Sector"),
        th("FY"),
        th("Peak exposure"),
        th("Description"),
        th("Investor country")
      )
    ),
    tbody(
      lapply(seq_len(nrow(miga_html)), function(i) {
        row <- miga_html[i, ]
        tr(
          td(row[["Proj. ID"]]),
          td(row[["Title"]]),
          td(row[["Sector"]]),
          td(as.character(row[["FY"]])),
          td(row[["Peak exposure"]]),
          td(HTML(as.character(row[["Description"]]))),
          td(row[["Investor country"]])
        )
      })
    )
  )
})
```

> MIGA uses **fiscal years** (July–June). FY2008 = July 2007 – June 2008. Gross exposure represents the maximum MIGA liability under issued guarantee contracts — not capital transferred to Costa Rica.
